name: Pyramiding

card.summary: A pattern of anabolic-steroid use in which the dose is ramped up to a mid-cycle peak and then tapered down, used by people seeking added muscle.
card.note: Anabolic steroids carry documented cardiovascular, liver, hormonal and psychiatric harms; the pattern itself has not been scientifically validated.

quick.overview:
Pyramiding is a way of structuring a cycle of anabolic androgenic steroids: the amount used climbs gradually to a peak around the middle of the cycle and then falls back toward zero. People using it are aiming for more muscle mass and a more muscular physique.

Users believe the gradual ramp gives the body time to adjust and the taper eases the drop-off at the end. The US National Institute on Drug Abuse states that the effects of pyramiding, cycling and plateauing have not been substantiated scientifically.
quick.how: Described in general terms, a cycle lasts roughly 6 to 12 weeks, rises to a peak, tapers, and may be followed by a drug-free period; it is often combined with other steroids ('stacking'). Training and diet continue throughout. This article does not describe amounts or products.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroids are associated with high blood pressure, blood clots, heart attack and stroke, liver damage, reduced sperm production and testicular shrinkage in men, masculinisation in women, and aggression, mood disorders and dependence. Non-medical use is illegal in many countries, and injection with unsterile equipment risks blood-borne infection.

lead: Pyramiding is a pattern of non-medical anabolic steroid use in which the dose is raised to a peak around the middle of a cycle and then lowered again, sometimes followed by a drug-free break. It is one of several cycle structures described in bodybuilding and weightlifting circles, alongside stacking and plateauing.[1]

The goal for most non-athlete users is a more muscular appearance. The US National Institute on Drug Abuse reports that appearance is the main reason many recreational weightlifters use steroids, and links use with muscle dysmorphia, the preoccupation with being too small.[1]

Proponents say the ramp lets the body adjust and the drug-free phase lets the hormonal system recover. NIDA states that the effects of pyramiding, cycling and plateauing have not been substantiated scientifically.[1]

chain: Dose ramped up then tapered across a cycle
Anabolic steroids raise muscle-building signalling alongside training
Greater muscle size and a larger-looking physique
angle.text: Users structure steroid cycles as a pyramid in the belief that it maximises muscle gain and limits side effects. The muscle-building effect belongs to the steroids; the pyramid pattern itself has not been tested.

infobox: Non-medical use illegal in many countries

paras: In NIDA's description, pyramiding means slowly escalating steroid use to a peak at mid-cycle and then gradually tapering toward the end of a 6 to 12 week cycle, sometimes followed by a drug-free period.[1] Cycling more generally means taking several doses over a set period, stopping, and restarting; stacking means combining two or more different steroids.[1]

Users and some coaches in bodybuilding communities say the ramp reduces side effects and the taper helps natural hormone production return. The idea that stacked or pyramided regimens give greater effects has not been scientifically tested, according to NIDA.[1]

NIDA lists cardiovascular effects (high blood pressure, clots, heart attack, stroke), liver damage including tumours and peliosis hepatis, reduced sperm production and testicular shrinkage in men, masculinisation in women, infection risk from shared injection equipment, and aggression, anxiety, mood disorders and withdrawal depression.[1] Wikipedia notes that prolonged androgen use temporarily suppresses natural testosterone production.[2]
